title: As search traffic dries up, Reddit announces it’s shifting to a logged-in experience
script:
Reddit is shifting to a primarily logged-in experience for its users.
CEO Steve Huffman confirms this change protects content from unauthorized AI scrapers.
The platform now forces sign-ins to prevent unauthorized data scraping by AI crawlers.
This move will strictly restrict third-party access to public threads.
This follows Reddit's sixty million dollar annual data licensing deal with Google.
Expect more aggressive prompts to create an account while browsing.
Would you keep using Reddit if you had to sign in?
